subject: Take-home prompt delivery — system design & inference task
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: James Martinez <j.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Take-home prompt delivery — system design & inference task

Hi James —

Thanks again for chatting with Marissa yesterday; we enjoyed the conversation. As discussed, please find the take-home prompt attached. High level: a short system-design + inference-quality task with an implementation component.

Quick logistics:
- Attachment: redwood-takehome-ml-inference.pdf (2 pages) — prompt, constraints, and submission checklist.
- Deadline: Sunday, Dec 6, 2026 23:59 PT. If you need an extension please let us know by end of day Friday (Nov 27).
- How to submit: Reply to this thread with a zip file containing your code, a README with run steps, and a short writeup (<=2 pages). If the artifact is large, share a Drive link.
- Environment: we expect Python 3.9+, Docker optional (see constraints in the doc). No GPU required — CPU-only runs must complete within 30 minutes on a 4-core machine.

Next steps for us: we will assign two reviewers (one hiring manager, one engineer) and block a 60-minute debrief slot for the week after the submission window closes.

Please reply to confirm you received the prompt.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Talent Partner, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: James Martinez <j.martinez@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Take-home prompt delivery — system design & inference task

Connor —

Got it, thanks. I confirm receipt and will start on this today. Two quick qs: 
1) Are there any hard limits on model size / quantization? The pdf mentions "model variant" but not a strict cap.
2) Should I include inference logs and token-level cost estimates, or is a short summary enough?

If helpful, I can aim to submit by Dec 5 to leave buffer.

Best,
James

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Thanks Connor — assigning reviewers now. Proposed reviewers: 
- Karthik Iyer (Senior Infra Engineer) — will evaluate implementation and runtime constraints.
- Markus Klein (ML Engineer) — will review design tradeoffs and quality tests.

I've attached a short reviewer guide and rubric (reviewer-guide.md). Proposed calendar windows for debriefs: 
- Wed, Dec 8, 10:00–11:00 PT (preferred)
- Thu, Dec 9, 15:00–16:00 PT (backup)

I'll create a shared Drive folder with submissions and rubrics once the candidate sends the artifact.

Perfect — thanks Neha. I added the two reviewers and created the calendar placeholders for Dec 8 / Dec 9. Two asks:

Connor / Neha —

Submitting my solution; zip attached (james_martinez_solution.zip). In the root README I included run steps, a short design rationale, and instructions to reproduce the results. I also included a small CSV with inference logs and an estimate of token-level cost under the assumptions in the prompt.
